thesis.counterparty: Passive limit-order liquidity providers (makers) quoting the illiquid alt book who have not yet re-priced off BTC's already-public move; they get adversely selected by flow that already knows BTC moved and rotates into the alt before the alt's own book catches up.
thesis.evidence: (1) Springer, 'Price Transmission from Bitcoin to Altcoins: High-Frequency Evidence and Implications for Trading Strategy' (Asia-Pacific Financial Markets, 2026) -- per the indexed abstract/summary: small-cap cryptocurrencies exhibit significant delayed responses to BTC price movements, with some assets showing correlation coefficients at a one-minute lag slightly higher than at lag-0 (lower liquidity -> slower reaction), unidirectional Granger-causality from BTC to ALTs, and a lag trading strategy using BTC's preceding returns as a leading indicator that outperforms buy-and-hold across market conditions. Note this source's own measured lag is ~1 minute (sub-bar for our 1h screen) and the paper reports large/medium-cap names reacting near-simultaneously -- so this thesis explicitly narrows the universe to small/mid-cap names and tests whether an aggregate, coarser (hourly) version of the same propagation mechanism still leaves an exploitable post-cost move, rather than assuming the paper's own 1-minute number is directly tradable at 1h resolution. (2) arxiv.org/abs/2506.08718, 'Price Discovery in Cryptocurrency Markets' -- opened abstract: for ETH, 'centralized markets typically lead in ETH price discovery' vs. Uniswap v2, and BTC futures 'tend to lead overall, however high-volatility periods produce mixed outcomes' (Hasbrouck Information Share / Gonzalo-Granger decomposition, 2024 event windows) -- corroborates the general mechanism (the most liquid/central venue leads, slower venues/assets catch up with a lag) that this thesis applies intra-venue (BTC leads other alts on the same book) rather than cross-venue, since the desk's load_data has no cross-exchange/DEX feed to trade the literal cross-venue version.
thesis.mechanism: Informed order flow trades the deepest, most-watched book first (BTC). Lower-liquidity alt order books are re-priced / arbed less continuously (fewer market makers watching them tick-by-tick), so a large BTC move propagates into alt prices with a measurable delay before the alt's own liquidity providers and arbitrageurs catch the book up. This is a same-venue, cross-asset attention/liquidity-provisioning lag, not a cross-exchange latency arb (the desk has no cross-venue data to trade that version -- see evidence).

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 2 (Short-horizon reversion, alt-vs-ETH, high-vol) bets on mean-reversion of an alt-vs-ETH spread on a short (~5m) horizon triggered by high volatility. This thesis bets on directional momentum continuation/catch-up of an alt following a large BTC move at 1h resolution -- opposite sign of bet (continuation, not reversion), different leader asset (BTC not ETH), and a different trigger (a lagged-propagation window, not a same-bar high-vol condition).

Row 5 (Market-neutral cross-sectional momentum) died because it needs a ~100-470-name basket for diversification and collapses to unreliable returns at 1-3 positions; it ranks/nets many names against each other. This thesis is not a basket or a cross-sectional ranking -- each alt is graded independently against its own BTC-triggered signal, so the breadth-dilution failure mode that killed row 5 does not structurally apply; n comes from pooling independent per-symbol trade counts, not from relative-strength ranking across a basket.

Row 13 (BTC-TSM(28,5)) trades BTC itself off BTC's own trailing price trend and fails to beat buy-and-hold. This thesis never takes a BTC position at all -- BTC's return is only an exogenous leading signal used to trade a *different* asset (the alt), which is a cross-asset propagation bet, not a single-asset trend-following bet.

thesis.prediction: In long_1h TRAIN-era data (universe below, BTC excluded), when BTC's trailing 3-bar (3h) return exceeds +/-150bps, the same-direction alt trade entered at the next bar's open and held up to 24 bars will show: (a) n>=30 trades with bootstrap CI95 of net bps (after C_BPS=11.5) excluding zero, and (b) observed win rate >= p*(200bps)=52.875% (fee_math.p_star). If either fails, the hourly-scale version of this propagation does not survive costs and the thesis is killed -- the mechanism is real at sub-hour granularity per the cited source but may simply resolve within the same 1h bar, leaving nothing to trade at this bar size.
thesis.signal_py:
screens/informed_flow_btc_alt_lag/signal.py (see file; reproduced): """informed_flow_btc_alt_lag -- BTC-led momentum propagation into slower-liquidity alts.

Mechanism: informed flow trades the deepest, most-watched book (BTC) first. Lower-
liquidity alt books are re-priced / arbed less continuously, so a large BTC move
propagates into alt prices with a measurable delay -- documented in the literature at
sub-hour granularity for small-cap names (see thesis source_urls). This signal tests
whether that propagation survives as an exploitable move at hourly-bar resolution, net
of Phemex's 11.5bp round-trip cost.

Rule (closed bars only, no lookahead):
- At each closed alt bar t, compute BTC's trailing BTC_LOOKBACK_BARS-bar (3h) return in
  bps, using only BTC bars with timestamp <= t (forward-filled onto the alt's own index --
  never a future BTC value).
- If BTC's trailing return > +LAG_THRESH_BPS  -> long the alt (bet on catch-up).
- If BTC's trailing return < -LAG_THRESH_BPS  -> short the alt.
- Otherwise flat.

Causality: btc_close.reindex(df.index, method='ffill') only ever pulls BTC values at or
before each timestamp in the (possibly truncated) df passed in; pct_change() looks
backward only. Re-running signals() on any prefix of df therefore reproduces identical
values at every shared timestamp -> passes screen.causality_check's whole-prefix
exact-equality test.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd

from research.swarm.lib import load_data as ld

BTC_LOOKBACK_BARS = 3       # BTC trailing-return window, in 1h bars (3h)
LAG_THRESH_BPS = 150.0      # BTC move (bps) required to trigger a propagation bet
DATASET = 'long_1h'
TIMEFRAME = '1h'


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    btc = ld.load_ohlcv('BTC', TIMEFRAME, era='train', dataset=DATASET)
    btc_close = btc['close']

    # Causal alignment: only BTC values at-or-before each alt bar's own timestamp.
    btc_aligned = btc_close.reindex(df.index, method='ffill')
    btc_ret_bps = btc_aligned.pct_change(BTC_LOOKBACK_BARS) * 10000.0

    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[btc_ret_bps > LAG_THRESH_BPS] = 1
    sig[btc_ret_bps < -LAG_THRESH_BPS] = -1
    sig = sig.fillna(0).astype(int)
    return sig

spec.doa_line: Kill if, at n>=30 train-era trades, bootstrap_ci.mean_ci of net bps (fee_math.C_BPS=11.5 applied) includes zero, or observed win rate < fee_math.p_star(200)=0.52875, or the two registered tp_bps robustness variants (+20%/-20% of 200bps) do not both keep the same net_bps_mean sign as the base case.
